caption:
Lulu works early starts and night shifts, on her feet all day. Making the same class every week just isn't happening.

It doesn't need to be the same day. Two sessions in any seven-day stretch is a good starting point, slotted into days off or before a later start. Pilates for the hips, trunk and upper back can help you feel more capable when lifting, pushing and turning.

After a run of nights, a lighter session focused on mobility and breathing often suits better. On busy weeks, five minutes at home of bridges, side-lying leg lifts and cat-cows keeps the habit going.

Our Pilates team at Hybrid Physio can build a program around your shifts. Book online via the link in bio.

General information only — not a substitute for an individual assessment.
